title: Nissan shuts down global vehicle diagnostics system after detecting unauthorized access, NYT reports
date_note: Start of the disruption as given by zn.ua (21 November 2026), relaying The New York Times; zn.ua says it was still unresolved on Friday, 20 November.
place: Japan (company's home country; dealers worldwide affected)
geo_basis: country: the article describes Nissan as a Japanese automaker; no site of the intrusion is stated
summary: Nissan temporarily shut down the global vehicle diagnostics system its dealers use after detecting unauthorized access to it, zn.ua reported on 21 November, relaying The New York Times. The disruption began on 13 November and was not fixed as of 20 November. Dealers cannot reprogram vehicle electronics or make duplicate keys, which may delay service for Nissan and Infiniti cars; Nissan has not said who was behind it, according to the report.
plain: Nissan switched off a worldwide system its dealers use to diagnose and reprogram cars after finding someone had got into it. Some repairs and spare keys for Nissan and Infiniti cars may be delayed.
exec: A dealer diagnostics system was taken offline after unauthorized access, delaying some Nissan and Infiniti repairs; a reminder that service tooling is attack surface.
impact: Dealers cannot reprogram vehicle electronics or make duplicate keys while the system is offline; routine maintenance continues, per Nissan's message to service centres as relayed by zn.ua.

key_findings: Nissan reported a temporary shutdown of its global vehicle diagnostics system after detecting unauthorized access.
The disruption began on 13 November and was still unresolved on 20 November.
Dealers cannot reprogram electronics or make duplicate keys; service for Nissan and Infiniti cars may be delayed.
